cases.title: Percent change from forecast 658 to actual 700
cases.notes: Exact value 6.382978723...%. Positive %CH = increase (p. 64). Example does NOT press CLR WORK first; it relies on #PD already being 1. Guidebook display carries a computed-value marker (*) that is not part of the numeric string.

cases.title: Entering OLD in the Percent Change worksheet
cases.notes: Entered-value marker (a small left triangle) accompanies the display in the guidebook; not part of the string.

cases.title: Entering NEW in the Percent Change worksheet
cases.notes: DOWN from OLD reaches NEW.

cases.title: Entering -7 as percent change
cases.notes: Keying over a just-computed value re-marks %CH as entered. Negative %CH = decrease (p. 64).

cases.title: New amount 7% below the 658 forecast
cases.notes: 658 x (1 - 0.07)^1 = 611.94 exactly. UP from %CH reaches NEW. Overwrites the previously entered NEW=700.

cases.title: Entering the stock purchase price 500 as OLD
cases.notes: OLD = present value in the compound-interest role mapping (p. 64). The example opens on 'Current value' without clearing.

cases.title: Entering the stock selling price 750 as NEW
cases.notes: NEW = future value in the compound-interest role mapping (p. 64). DOWN from OLD reaches NEW.

cases.title: Entering #PD = 5 periods
cases.notes: DOWN DOWN from NEW passes %CH and lands on #PD.

cases.title: Annual growth rate: 500 to 750 over 5 years
cases.notes: Exact 100*((750/500)^(1/5)-1) = 8.44717712...%. This case is the arbiter proving #PD is an EXPONENT in the p.81 formula, which the vector rendering flattens to a trailing factor.

cases.title: CLR WORK in the Percent Change worksheet zeroes OLD
cases.notes: Display carries no entered/computed marker after a clear.

cases.title: Entering the original cost 100 as OLD
cases.notes: OLD = cost in the cost-sell-markup role mapping (p. 64). This example is the one in the chapter that clears the worksheet first.

cases.title: Entering the selling price 125 as NEW
cases.notes: NEW = selling price in the cost-sell-markup role mapping (p. 64). Same numeric pair as the Profit Margin example on p. 71, but that one yields MAR = 20 against the selling price while this yields %CH = 25 against the cost.

cases.title: Markup from cost 100 to selling price 125
cases.notes: CRITICAL DISCREPANCY ARBITER: the p.63 reset table prints #PD default = 0, but this example clears the worksheet and enters only OLD and NEW, then gets 25.00. That is only reachable if CLR WORK leaves #PD = 1 (matching the p.64 prose). The printed default table is wrong; #PD clears to 1. Markup is measured against cost, unlike the Profit Margin worksheet's MAR.

cases.title: Entering a 15% nominal rate
cases.notes: NOM and EFF are both entered as ANNUAL rates in percent (p. 67).

cases.title: Setting quarterly compounding (C/Y = 4)
cases.notes: DOWN DOWN from NOM passes EFF and lands on C/Y. C/Y here is enter-only and is the Interest Conversion worksheet's own variable (default 1); 2ND CLR WORK in this worksheet deliberately does not touch it (p. 67).

cases.title: Effective rate for 15% nominal compounded quarterly
cases.notes: Exact 100*((1+0.15/4)^4 - 1) = 15.86504150390625% -> rounds to 15.87. FORMULA ARBITER: the p.80 printed EFF equation reads 'ln(x DIVIDE 1)'; the '+ 1' reading is the only one producing 15.87 (the printed '÷ 1' reading yields ln(0.0375), i.e. approximately -100). The example wins. The printed equation also flattens the exponent of e and drops its closing parenthesis.

cases.title: Date worksheet opens on the default DT1
cases.notes: Default shown only on a freshly reset machine (2ND RESET ENTER) or after 2ND CLR WORK in this worksheet. Dates display MM-DD-YYYY with an unpadded month.

cases.title: Entering DT1 = September 4, 2003
cases.notes: US entry format is MM.DDYY -- 9.0403 is one keyed token. Two-digit year 03 maps into the 1980-2079 window (p. 81). Keying MM.DDYYYY instead raises Error 6 (p. 85). Note the day is zero-padded on output but the month is not.

cases.title: Entering DT2 = November 1, 2003
cases.notes: DOWN from DT1 reaches DT2. The calculator assumes DT1 is earlier than DT2 (p. 68).

cases.title: Actual/actual day-count setting is displayed
cases.notes: DOWN DOWN from DT2 passes DBD and lands on the day-count setting slot. This is a setting, not a number: the display is the bare method name with no '=' and no value. The example does not press 2ND SET because ACT is already the default.

cases.title: Days between Sept 4, 2003 and Nov 1, 2003 (actual/actual)
cases.notes: 26 remaining days in September + 31 in October + 1 in November = 58. UP from the ACT slot returns to DBD. Displayed with the current DEC setting, hence '58.00' not '58'. Under the 30/360 method the same pair would give 57, but the guidebook does not print that comparison.

cases.title: Profit Margin worksheet opens on CST
cases.notes: The guidebook shows 0.00 here rather than 'Current value', implying a freshly reset/cleared machine. There is no auto-clear on worksheet entry.

cases.title: Entering selling price 125
cases.notes: DOWN from CST reaches SEL.

cases.title: Entering a 20% gross profit margin
cases.notes: MAR is a percentage of SELLING PRICE, not of cost (p. 70).

cases.title: Cost from selling price 125 at 20% margin
cases.notes: 125 x (1 - 0.20) = 100 exactly. Matches the p.81 printed formula with no sign flip. UP UP from MAR walks back through SEL to CST.

cases.title: Entering fixed costs of 3,000
cases.notes: Thousands separator is present in the displayed string. FC is entered as a positive magnitude; the formula subtracts it.

cases.title: Entering unit variable cost of 15
cases.notes: DOWN from FC reaches VC.

cases.title: Entering unit price of 20
cases.notes: DOWN from VC reaches P.

cases.title: Profit left at zero for a breakeven solve
cases.notes: The example steps onto PFT and leaves it. PFT = 0 is what makes the subsequent Q a breakeven quantity (p. 71). Display carries no entered marker because nothing was keyed. This case assumes PFT is already 0 from a prior reset/clear -- the worksheet is not auto-cleared on entry.

cases.title: Breakeven quantity: FC 3000, VC 15, P 20, PFT 0
cases.notes: Q = (FC + PFT)/(P - VC) = 3000/5 = 600 exactly. Matches the printed PFT = PQ - (FC + VCQ) with no sign inversion. Computing Q with P = VC divides by zero -> Error 1.

cases.title: Clearing memory 4 by storing zero
cases.notes: Four DOWN presses from M0 reach M4. There is no single-memory clear key; 2ND CLR WORK here would wipe ALL TEN memories (p. 73).

cases.title: Storing 95 in memory 4
cases.notes: Keying a value with a memory displayed and pressing ENTER replaces the stored value. All memory variables are enter-only (p. 72).

cases.title: Memory arithmetic: add 65
cases.notes: 95 + 65 = 160. Operator key, operand, ENTER applies in place and redisplays the memory.

cases.title: Memory arithmetic: subtract 30
cases.notes: 160 - 30 = 130. Stored value is the LEFT operand.

cases.title: Memory arithmetic: multiply by 95
cases.notes: 130 x 95 = 12,350. Thousands separator present in the display string.

cases.title: Memory arithmetic: divide by 65
cases.notes: 12,350 / 65 = 190. Confirms operand ordering: stored / keyed, not keyed / stored.

cases.title: Memory arithmetic: raise to the 2nd power
cases.notes: 190^2 = 36,100 -- confirms the stored value is the BASE and the keyed value the exponent, not the reverse (2^190 would overflow). Y^X with a negative stored value and a non-integer, non-inverse-integer exponent raises Error 2 (p. 84).
